b: Protein is essential to nearly every biological function in the body. We have discussed at length the importance of consuming enough of it, especially with age, when muscle becomes less responsive to dietary protein and the resulting loss of muscle can contribute to frailty. Yet, in apparent contradiction, decades of animal research suggests that restricting protein can extend lifespan. A recent review article1 has drawn renewed attention to this possibility, inspiring headlines that low-protein diets may be better for longevity.

But “protein restriction” is not a single, clearly defined intervention. Some studies lower total protein, while others selectively restrict individual amino acids—often severely. Although some rodent experiments report meaningful lifespan or metabolic benefits, the effects are inconsistent and can come with substantial costs. Before we kick our high-protein diets to the curb, it’s worth looking closely at what was restricted, which animals benefited, what trade-offs accompanied those gains, and whether any of it translates to humans.
